summary: Import native Nexus cold-start scene data into the connected TileLang LBVH, general collision and ordinary-joint frame program.
regressions: Real CPU and Metal uploads are byte-identical for offset multiple colliders, separate parent/body indices, parentless mesh and colored prismatic joints with limits and motors.
Twelve native frame/manifest tests, three real Metal upload tests and six runtime validation tests pass; both reference and native strict clippy pass.
Reject cross-batch parents, joint writer aliasing, invalid native counts and schedules, nonfinite physical geometry, changed fixed bodies and capacity guards.
The mesh-contact/joint one-frame diagnostic passes C parity and independent geometry/response checks without tolerance changes; the registered multi-target runtime matrix remains required.
differences: Native upload is a cold start, not continuation. Generic scene specialization retains bounded coloring, Coulomb friction, finite frame traces and explicit pair capacity. Public backend selection, unrestricted scene lifecycle and remaining solver variants are still in progress.

The CPU-only native export uses the pinned noalias-disabled environment, LLVM probe and an additional build guard. Metal-only native execution remains on its separate toolchain. CPU support adds corosensei and its Windows support dependencies without upgrading existing locked packages.

Unused mesh BVH leaf slots may contain exactly [+inf,-inf] bounds from native flattening; only a validation copy normalizes these proven-unused slots. Kernel input bits remain unchanged. Primitive vertices and non-leaf bounds must remain finite.
Generalized joint validation previously assumed three fixture colors and would interpret a one-color upload guard as a color range. It now respects the actual count and retains exact alias rejection.

No Rust shader arithmetic or mirrored shader files changed. The host CPU feature split and conservative source envelope require full revalidation. Native build guards and integration tests are now included in that envelope.
Ascend vendor compilation, device execution, synchronization and performance remain unqualified.
